answer.rationale: Rollback is excluded (security patch must not ship-revert). The degradation is confined to the primary region, which makes regional_failover tempting per memory_b2, but failing over a write-heavy primary at daily settlement peak risks losing in-flight writes to replication lag — directly against the primary objective of no lost customer writes. The release correlation is suspicious but cannot be acted on, so the most likely mechanism under peak write load is capacity saturation. Memory_b3 supports that provisioning headroom absorbed a heavy write surge without impact. Adding capacity is the only intervention that relieves write-path pressure without risking write loss or violating compliance. I verify b3 to confirm the original record covers write-path (not just queue) saturation. Uncertainty remains: if the new release introduced a write-path inefficiency, capacity may only mask it; that must be investigated in the next window.
